headline: Pretrained embeddings are reused across protein, RNA, and genomic prediction tasks
label: Representation Learning For Biomolecular Prediction
summary: Sequence-based transformers and language models are being trained, distilled, and scaled for binding, specificity, and fitness prediction.
synthesis: The dominant thread is reuse of learned representations of biomolecular sequences and structures across prediction tasks. ZeroFold derives protein-RNA binding affinity from sequence using pre-structural Boltz-2 embeddings and the PRADB dataset of 2,621 pairs. ImmSET, a sequence-based transformer, scales with data for TCR-pMHC specificity, while AINN-P1, a 167M-parameter attention-free mLSTM protein language model, reports a 0.441 average Spearman on ProteinGym. Other items apply the same pattern to embedding-level distillation of a genomic model for mRNA, scaling and quantization of single-cell foundation models, and RNA modification prediction with an evolutionary RNA language model. What is new is the transfer of pretrained knowledge into compact or specialized models: distillation shrinks a genomic model roughly 200-fold, and co-distillation across ESM family members aims to compress their collective knowledge into a single protein language model.
